REQUESTED BY: Erik Larsen, DO

CONSULT DATE: 09/04/2018



Pulmonary Medicine Consultation

The patient is being seen at the Orthopedic floor.

REASON FOR CONSULTATION: Preop evaluation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: Mrs. Munkel is an 86-year-old female who

I know for many years ago. She has bronchial asthma and had done

quite well using only albuterol on an as-needed basis. Unfortunately,

she fell at home, sustained a fracture of the left elbow. She comes

back for elective surgery. Preop evaluation is requested. A chest

x-ray shows chronic changes. No gross infiltrates on an AP as well as

lateral view. Last time she used her albuterol was several months

ago. Her asthma is usually triggered by allergies, change of season,

as well as upper respiratory tract infection.

The patient says she has undergone a cardiac evaluation in view of her

risk factors.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, hiatal

hernia, chronic bronchial asthma. She also has chronic spinal

stenosis.

ALLERGIES: INCLUDE MORPHINE AND MOTRIN.

PERSONAL AND SOCIAL HISTORY: She was a homemaker. Lives at home with

her husband. Never smoked. Never drank.

FAMILY HISTORY: Noncontributory.

MEDICATIONS: Medications taken on a regular basis include:

1. Vitamin B12.

2. Turmeric capsules.

3. Levothyroxine 50 mcg once a day.

4. Metformin 500 mg 1 tab daily.

5. Metoprolol tartrate 25 mg one half tablet daily.

6. Vitamin D3.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: GENERAL SURVEY: This is an elderly female who

appears her stated age. She is awake, alert, not in distress. VITAL

SIGNS: Revealed the following: Temperature is 98.9, blood pressure

156/76, heart rate 84, respiratory rate 22. SKIN: Warm to touch. No

petechiae. No ecchymosis. HEENT: Normocephalic. no alar flaring.

NECK: Supple. There is small hematoma of the left chin area.

CHEST/LUNGS: Clear breath sounds anteriorly, diminished at the bases,

but no crackles. Examination is limited because of the extensive

immobilization of left upper extremity. HEART: Heart sounds are

distinct. Regular rate. ABDOMEN: Soft. No organomegaly.

EXTREMITIES: No pedal edema. No calf tenderness. Pulses are intact.

Left upper extremity is immobilized.

PERTINENT INFORMATION: WBC count 7000, hemoglobin 12.4, hematocrit

36.3, platelet count 185,000. BUN 18, creatinine 1.01. Blood gas on

room air shows a pH of 7.02, PCO2 of 36, pO2 of 77, saturations 96%.

ASSESSMENT:

1. LEFT ELBOW FRACTURE.

2. BRONCHIAL ASTHMA, STABLE, MILD, VERY INTERMITTENT TYPE.

3. DIABETES.

4. HYPERTENSION.

5. HYPERLIPIDEMIA.

6. LEFT ELBOW FRACTURE.

PLAN: From Pulmonary point of view, she is 100% cleared for planned

surgery. We will offer albuterol on as-needed basis. She will

require incentive spirometry postoperative. Pain medications have

been reviewed. We will start with some baseline IV fluids.

Thank you for this consultation. We will follow the patient with

you.

she also landed on her left jaw area and again unfortunately I do not

done. At this point, the patient denies having any chest pain. No

syncopal episode. No GU complaint. No burning. No fever. No chills. No

URI symptoms. No diarrhea. No bleeding episode. No constipation,

though in the past, the patient has a history of infection of the

history of obesity, history of palpitation, asthma.

The patient has seen Dr. Meily in the past for pulmonary and Dr. Asu

Rustemli from Cardio. History of spinal stenosis, osteoarthritis,

history of left forearm surgery done by Dr. Semet, history of

diverticulitis. Diabetes, on metformin; history of hyperlipidemia;

history of kidney stone with mild hydronephrosis in 2011; hiatal

hernia; history of anxiety; dysphagia, was seen by Dr. Rustemli 2017.

At that time, the echo showed ejection fraction was normal, showed

mildly dilated LA and mild MR i do not have any report of any stress

test done recently. The patient also has history of hypothyroidism.

MEDICATIONS: Reconciled. Please refer to the chart for the full

details of this med reconciliation.

Unfortunately, her last bone density is not available, though she has

a known family history of osteoporosis and known family history of

breast cancer.

LABORATORY DATA: Labs of the patient, pending. EKG, pending. Blood

gas, pending. Chest x-ray, pending.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: VITAL SIGNS: Blood pressure 122/65, respiratory

rate 18, pulse rate of 80, temperature is 98.3, and saturation, we

didnt do it. GENERAL: The patient is awake, little anxious. HEENT:

Pupils reactive. The patient has a left jaw bruising. Also, gums of

the patient noted to have some swelling, but no obvious bleeding in

the mouth. Tongue is midline. Speech is clear. LUNGS: Clear anteriorly

and posteriorly. CARDIAC: S1 and S2, regular. Positive for soft

murmur. ABDOMEN: Soft and nontender. on palpation no tenderness.

EXTREMITIES: The patient has an Ace wrap on whole left upper

extremity. No clubbing, no cyanosis, no edema. Good pedal pulse. No

obvious carotid bruit. NEURO: By the way, the patient is nonfocal,

except for the left side.

So, Mrs. Munkel Joan is going for left proximal ulnar surgery under

Dr. Larsen. Again, discussed with Dr. Larsen. He claims he has all the

CAT scan report, though I will ask the staff if we can get it from

Brick Hospital. The patient wants to be full code. She wants her

daughter to be the first call. She claims as her husband is starting

to have memory issue. She will have a full code. DVT prophylaxis has

been ordered. Incentive spirometry. Other testing at this point is

pending. So far, the patient is not clear, awaiting all the workup. A

urine culture has also been requested. Accu-Cheks has been requested

also with sliding scale. Medication reconciled.

I will be following the case with you.
